agents.note:
US-513 DONE (Sprint 69 / V0.29.24, 7/11). Also committed US-512's sprint.json+progress.txt, which the prior iteration left UNCOMMITTED -- the TD-059 stall for the THIRD consecutive story (US-504b, US-505, now US-512). The pattern is stable: the WORK lands, the close-out commit is what gets dropped. If you boot into a dirty tree whose sprint.json/progress.txt already describe a story marked passes:true, that is this stall -- verify and COMMIT, do not re-implement.

US-513 WAS A RESEARCH STORY AND THE HEADLINE IS A NEGATIVE: origin UNPROVABLE, project EXONERATED, mitigation INSUFFICIENT (now fixed). I did not name a culprit for the 07-03 soft-block because all three forensic sources are gone -- the saved-state file was OVERWRITTEN by the 07-31 recovery (mtime 07-31 20:26, and rm -f /var/lib/systemd/rfkill/* is in the Pi's bash_history), the journal retains only back to 07-26, and bash_history covers only the recovery session (and never captures agent commands at all: ssh host "cmd" is non-interactive and does not append to history). Guessing a cause there would have been a fabrication dressed as a finding.

WHAT IS PROVEN: no project code or deploy path can produce a soft-block. Zero rfkill block / nmcli radio off / hciconfig down / systemctl stop bluetooth / bluetoothctl power off in src+scripts+deploy; every radio verb the repo ships is restorative. Consistent with Atlas's manual-artifact hypothesis, corroborated but NOT proven by commit ad59561 (a live-Pi BT 'pairing-saga' session dated exactly 07-03).

THE FIND THE NEXT AGENT SHOULD LEARN FROM -- auditing the safety net turned up a live defect. eclipse-rfkill-unblock.service ordered itself After=systemd-rfkill (the PRODUCER half, which its own header calls 'the fix') and Before= nothing. Neither rfcomm-bind nor eclipse-obd declared any relation to it, so all three could start concurrently -- and on the Pi's 07-31 boot rfcomm-bind and the unblock BOTH entered active at 20:25:59, the SAME SECOND. On a boot where a block is actually saved that race binds /dev/rfcomm0 to a dark adapter while every unit reads 'active'. Fixed: Before=rfcomm-bind eclipse-obd (Before=, never Wants= -- order the consumers, never pull them in). NOT yet on the Pi; it lands on the next routine deploy via the cmp -s-guarded install step.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT (sixth sighting this sprint of the two-correct-halves shape, after US-494/499/502/503/505): the existing test asserted the ordering against unit_manifest.START_ORDER, a hand-ordered PYTHON TUPLE. unit_manifest's header says its ordering is 'grounded in the units' own declarations, NOT invented' -- and this was the one entry with no declaration behind it. A manifest cannot order boot. GENERAL LESSON: when a test asserts an ordering/dependency, check whether it reads the artifact that ENFORCES the behaviour or a second copy that merely DESCRIBES it.

SHIPPED PREVENTION: tests/deploy/test_no_radio_disable_in_project.py -- repo-wide static guard making the exoneration a standing invariant instead of a point-in-time audit (US-512's guard is runtime-only and covers just two helpers). Two design notes worth reusing: (a) its SELF-TEST caught on the first run that a whitespace-only separator misses argv-list form subprocess.run(["rfkill","block"]) -- always give a static guard a self-test, or a rotted regex passes forever; (b) whole-line # comments must be stripped, because bluetooth_helper.py and obd_connection.py DOCUMENT the forbidden commands and a raw scanner flags the prose explaining the rule (US-501's lesson, hit again).

DECLINED ON PURPOSE: testing whether bluetoothctl power off can itself save a block -- that needs a radio disabled on the car Pi + a reboot, against the standing 'never disable a radio on the Pi remotely' rule (07-19 nmcli stranding) with an engine-on drive owed. Routed to PM for a bench Pi / CIO-present run. Also routed: the Pi's ~1-week journal retention is the sole reason this RCA cannot close harder.

Green in-loop: tests/deploy + tests/pi/ops = exit 0 (374 + 25 new, zero skips); ruff clean. Commits 1502e0d (US-512 bookkeeping recovery), 0341e6d (US-513).

SPRINT STATE: 7 done (US-501/502/503/504b/505/512/513). Remaining: US-504a (needs-ruling, BLOCKED on 2 rulings -- PM/Atlas orphan policy + Spool gate/band overlap; do NOT start), US-517 home-location config, US-518 sync re-anchor, US-521 gyro-fused pitch. Next pickup by priority is US-517.
